newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs steady-off $1.00 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs steady-off $1.00 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs sold steady to $1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by further sharp declines in pork prices Tuesday, livestock dealers said.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold down $1.00 at $48.00 to $48.50 in the country and $49.50 to $50.00 at plants. Illinois hogs sold steady with Tuesday at $49.00 to $50.00 in the country and $51.00 to $51.50 at plants.
Indiana hogs sold down $0.50 at $49.50 to $50.00 in the country and $50.50 to $51.00 at plants. Ohio hogs sold down $0.50 at $47.00 to $47.50 in the country and $49.00 to $49.50 at plants.
Packers were not aggressively buying hogs because lower pork prices continued to push packer operating margins into unprofitable territory, livestock dealers said.
"The boys are not real crazy about them (hogs) right now," one central Iowa hog buyer said.

Estimated gross cutout values of a 175-lb hog carcass on Tuesday were quoted down $1.72 to $1.85 per cwt, with the Number 2 carcass value down $1.80 at $68.09, USDA said. The Number 2 value had fallen $2.85, or about four percent, from the same period a week ago, USDA statistics showed.
